reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker or PD data reported to confirm durvalumab engaged PD-L1 or bevacizumab engaged VEGFA. Target engagement must be inferred from trial design assumptions. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers reported to confirm checkpoint blockade activated T-cell immunity or that bevacizumab inhibited angiogenesis. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: All primary endpoints failed across all cohorts - OS-12 was 60% in cohort A, PFS-6 ranged from 15.2-19.4% in cohorts B/B2/B3, and OS-6 was 36.4% in cohort C. No p-values reported but effect sizes suggest poor outcomes. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This appears to be an adequately powered multi-cohort study with 159 patients and 156-week duration. The failure appears to be mechanistic rather than operational.

failure_modes.evidence: Glioblastoma is known to be immunologically 'cold' with poor T-cell infiltration and an immunosuppressive microenvironment that may not respond well to checkpoint blockade. The blood-brain barrier also limits drug penetration.
While no biomarker data is available, the consistent failure across all cohorts including combination arms suggests the mechanism may not have engaged effectively in this CNS tumor context.
